request: Test temperature 1.2 on the exact capped four-case fixture previously used at 0.6 and 0.85, then test its previously strong repetition-penalty 1.2 variant separately.
interpretation_notes: Value-equivalent output with wrong JSON scalar types is not a fully correct tool call. Original exact contract scores remain unchanged.

The repetition-penalty 1.2 follow-up returns two actual calls, but code revision is a string instead of an integer, and deployment revision/boolean/null are strings instead of their expected types. The differing fields are listed per case.
The repetition-penalty 1.1 follow-up returns four completed direct reports with correct values after the documented order representation normalization, but emits no actual tool calls.
These completed synthetic requests do not establish a fix for native long-context stalls or other runtime failures. Production defaults remain at the previously activated profile.

scoring.correct_tool_contract: The actual parsed tool call must have the expected name and exact expected arguments, under the original scorer.
scoring.reported_data_exact: Expected report data appears exactly in visible JSON or parsed tool arguments; this alone does not pass the tool-call contract.
scoring.order_normalization: Only deployment_report planned_order may normalize a letter string to an array; the fixture did not explicitly specify its representation. This remains separate from strict contract scoring.
scoring.scalar_normalization: An additional diagnostic uniformly converts integer strings and the strings true/false/null only where the expected synthetic field has that type. Each conversion is listed. This distinguishes correct values with wrong types from wrong values; it does not pass or alter the actual tool-call contract.
scoring.completed_before_cap: The response finished without exhausting its output budget, independent of correctness.

limitations: One four-case batch per temperature and one seed are limited evidence, not a universal sampler ranking.
The 1.2 follow-up ran later, after production activity and a backend restart since the original two arms; runtime/process state is not perfectly paired.
Fresh cache salts and recorded metrics measure cache/isolation behavior; they do not eliminate all process-state confounds.
Batch time includes prompt processing and variable-length reasoning/output; it is not fixed-work throughput.
Synthetic roughly 20k cases do not reproduce the earlier 96k native incident or establish its cause.
Small synthetic sample; absence of short loops is not proof of a long-session fix.
Open design format checks are separate from qualitative human/agent review.
One shared server process and fixed seeds do not eliminate all order or runtime-state effects.
Elapsed times include prompt processing and varying output lengths; not fixed-work throughput.
Isolation uses idle gauges and completed-request/token accounting; no independent admission counter.
